ruledBy: Astra editorial review, adopted as Al's ruling (his instruction, 2026-09-05; veto list: none)
note: KEEP and FIX (fixed wording) are kept. KILL is held as `unruled`, NOT rejected — Al ruled that explicitly, so no downstream step may treat a KILL as struck. New-lines CSV rows are kept with source astra-new. astraTime is Astra's own visual reading of the hour and does not override the photograph's rotation slot.

kept.text: Your alarm still expects you to get up.
kept.fixedFrom: The rain started before the alarm did, and the gumboots were ready.

kept.text: Your school shoes will need their own bath.
Uniform on. Spare uniform suddenly makes sense.

unruled.text: Two under one umbrella: the first maths problem of the school day, solved.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: counts the pictured children under their umbrella.

unruled.text: The puddles are claiming the pavement one slab at a time.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: pavement description with decorative personification.

kept.text: You've apologised for being late. Start again.
The first meeting may have to start without you.
You left early. So did absolutely everyone else.

unruled.text: The mountain has its head in the weather and the traffic has its lights on.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: inventories mountain, weather and headlights.

unruled.text: The wiper is on its ten-thousandth swipe and the rain has not blinked.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: narrates the visible wiper instead of the reader.

kept.text: The washing can go out before you change your mind.
Shoes on. You have run out of excuses already.

unruled.text: The rain finished at five and left the whole street polished for the sunrise.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: polished sunrise caption invents a completion time.

unruled.text: Wet tar plus sunrise equals a street made of gold, briefly.
unruled.reason: R2 and R5 fail: postcard arithmetic, no human consequence.

unruled.text: Somebody ordered rain for the night and sun for the morning, and it was delivered.
unruled.reason: R1 and R5 fail: personified forecast still repeats the conditions.

kept.text: Car washing can stay at the bottom of your list.
Another cup, then. The errands can wait.

unruled.text: The rain is on the glass and the coffee is on the sill: Sunday is sorted.
unruled.reason: R5 and R6 fail: mug caption invents Sunday morning.

unruled.text: That window has the best programme on this morning and it is just rain.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: window caption dressed as television.

unruled.text: Steady, straight-down, all-morning rain: the kind the garden actually drinks.
unruled.reason: R1 fails: forecast description offers gardening commentary, no turn.

kept.text: Your umbrella warranty has some explaining to do.
kept.fixedFrom: Somewhere an umbrella just turned inside out. Moment of silence.

kept.text: Your expensive umbrella has chosen a short career.
Hair done. That was money well spent.

unruled.text: The umbrella lost, the kids won, and the rain takes full credit for both.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes the exact umbrella-and-children tableau.

unruled.text: Same rain, four verdicts: one against, three strongly in favour.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: witty headcount remains a caption of visible reactions.

kept.text: You said wash the car, which leaves room for debate.
Plans made. Several of them now need a lift.

unruled.text: The street is called Water Stilte and today it is taking the name literally.
unruled.reason: R5 and R7 fail: place-name wordplay captions this specific street.

unruled.text: That is not a river; that is Monday's road, repurposed.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: flooded-road description invents Monday.

unruled.text: Enough rain and somebody in this country will always find the ski rope.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: repeats the photograph's ski-rope gag.

kept.text: You can tell who will be doing the washing later.
Spare clothes packed. You forgot your own.

unruled.text: One good storm and the street gets a public swimming pool.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes the street puddle as a swimming pool.

unruled.text: The rain made the puddle; the puddle made the afternoon.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: picturesque sentiment describes the children's afternoon.

unruled.text: Six raincoats, one puddle, zero regrets: the rain knows its audience.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: raincoat inventory and borrowed zero-regrets slogan.

kept.text: Perhaps skip the scenic route home tonight.
One last stop. Make it the shop with a roof.

unruled.text: The rain found the one person at this robot without a roof.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes the roofless cyclist beside the car.

unruled.text: There is dry, there is wet, and there is cycling-at-a-red-robot wet.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: categories merely label the cyclist's visible predicament.

unruled.text: The helmet has a gutter now. It did not come with one.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: the helmet joke remains an image caption.

kept.text: Your supper plans have moved a little closer home.
Visitors expected. They can knock twice.

unruled.text: Rain in front, sunset behind: the Cape doing both of its moods at once.
unruled.reason: R5 and R7 fail: local landscape postcard.

unruled.text: The umbrella is old, the routine is older, and the rain changes neither.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: romanticises the pictured man's umbrella routine.

unruled.text: Lion's Head is catching the last light and the Bo-Kaap is catching the rain.
unruled.reason: R5 and R7 fail: tourist landmarks replace the reader.

kept.text: Remember the washing, now that you're eating supper?
Home at last. Now to negotiate with the dog.

unruled.text: The pot plant is getting the good stuff straight from the source tonight.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: narrates the plant receiving rain.

unruled.text: Joburg summer rain: arrives at five, soaks everything, gone by supper.
unruled.reason: R1 and R7 fail: local weather claim replaces a joke.

unruled.text: The balcony is doing its own rain gauge, and it reads: plenty.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: balcony puddle description, no human consequence.

kept.text: You can skip the long goodbye at the gate tonight.
Keys first. Being polite can happen inside.

unruled.text: Every neon sign in the street is being doubled on the wet tar tonight.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: wet-road reflections are already visible.

unruled.text: The coffee is deluxe, the books are shut, and the rain owns the street.
unruled.reason: R5 and R7 fail: shop-sign wordplay depends on this street.

unruled.text: The mountain has disappeared into the weather and left the signs in charge.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: landscape personification adds no reader consequence.

kept.text: An extra hour in bed would have cost the alarm nothing.
Time to get up. The roof has been up for hours.

unruled.text: Rain out here is an event; the whole veld will smell of it by seven.
unruled.reason: R1 and R7 fail: rural rain appreciation depends on location.

unruled.text: The road is running like a river and nobody here is complaining.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: flood caption assigns everybody an unearned opinion.

unruled.text: This is the rain the stoep chairs have been facing all year.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: romantic stoep-chair caption, no ordinary decision.

kept.text: The last two metres to the gate are the wettest of the whole trip.
The school run slows down. The bell doesn't.
kept.fixedFrom: Rain on a school morning slows everything down except the bell.

kept.text: The school still wants them there, unfortunately.
Lunch packed. Now to waterproof the child.

unruled.text: The umbrella is doing its first shift of the day at the school gate.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: narrates the pictured umbrella's school-gate job.

kept.text: You can start by moving car washing off the list.
First errand. Already considering a postponement.

unruled.text: The puddle has rings on it, which means this is not finished.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: explains visible puddle rings.

unruled.text: The road to the house is currently a mirror with a gate across it.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: mirror metaphor captions the driveway.

unruled.text: One night of proper rain and the driveway has joined the water table.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes driveway flooding through technical phrasing.

kept.text: Tea tastes better when your socks aren't involved.
Tea, then. Make it long enough to feel your toes.

unruled.text: The site turned to mud an hour ago and the shift goes on anyway.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: narrates the worker continuing in mud.

unruled.text: Rain on a building site: everything gets heavier and nobody gets softer.
unruled.reason: R2 fails: hardship-as-toughness slogan could advertise workwear.

unruled.text: The hard hat has become a gutter and the work has not stopped once.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: pictured hard-hat predicament remains the whole joke.

kept.text: The cat would like to speak to whoever booked this.
Door open. The dog would prefer a second opinion.

unruled.text: The cat has taken the rain personally, as the cat takes most things.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: amused cat description still captions its visible expression.

unruled.text: Dry spot found; dignity pending; the rain shows no sign of apologising.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: narrates the cat's shelter and expression.

unruled.text: One dry square metre in the whole yard, and it is occupied.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: directly describes the occupied dry patch.

kept.text: You might be working from home by popular demand.
Shop later. The last biscuit will have to stretch.

unruled.text: That is not driving anymore; that is low-altitude boating.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: flooded-car caption uses a familiar boating comparison.

unruled.text: One cloudburst and the whole street joined the storm-water system.
unruled.reason: R1 and R5 fail: repeats the condition and flooded street.

unruled.text: Every driveway on this street is a jetty until the drains catch up.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: driveway-as-jetty metaphor describes the visible flood.

kept.text: Everyone on this road just became a very careful person.
Nobody misses the driver you were yesterday.
Radio down. Apparently your eyes need the help.

unruled.text: Brake lights first, road second, everything else on trust.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: visibility inventory offers no earned human turn.

unruled.text: The wipers are on max and it's still not enough.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: literally describes the wipers' visible inadequacy.

kept.text: The gap between the stoep and the gate has never looked wider.
Eight metres to the car. Apparently a journey.
kept.fixedFrom: The umbrella is about to earn its whole year's keep in eight metres.

kept.text: All this for bread you weren't sure you needed.
Supper is ready. Getting everyone home is next.

unruled.text: He has checked the sky twice and the sky has not changed its answer.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: narrates the pictured man's sky-checking.

kept.text: Supper can wait. Apparently it has to.
kept.fixedFrom: The rain added an hour to the drive home and everyone saw it coming.

kept.text: You could have cooked supper by now. Twice.
kept.fixedFrom: The commute just became a team sport.

kept.text: Your family may have to eat without your commentary.
You said nearly home. That was a while ago.

unruled.text: Ten thousand brake lights and one mountain refusing to watch.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: brake-light and mountain personification remains scenery.

kept.text: Find a towel before anyone starts asking about work.
Shoes off. The whole household agrees on this.

unruled.text: The jacket gave up somewhere between the car and the gate.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes the pictured soaked jacket.

unruled.text: He made it home; the dry parts of him did not.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: neat contrast still captions the drenched arrival.

unruled.text: The hallway is getting its own weather report, drip by drip.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: narrates the hallway drips already pictured.

kept.text: Five more minutes in the car seems reasonable.
kept.fixedFrom: The rain gets five more minutes, and honestly, it can have them.

kept.text: You can call this sitting in the car some me time.
Nearly inside. An excellent place to reconsider.

unruled.text: There is no rush that survives weather like this, and she knows it.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: assigns serenity to the pictured woman.

unruled.text: Watching the rain from the driver's seat: free, dry, and weirdly good.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: directly labels the driver's visible activity.

kept.text: You can take your time getting home tonight.
Missed bedtime. The children have not.

unruled.text: Every light in town has gone soft at the edges tonight.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: night-light description gives no human consequence.

unruled.text: Night rain maths: half the visibility, double the concentration, triple the respect.
unruled.reason: R1 and R3 fail: condition opener introduces earnest driving advice.

unruled.text: Wet tar doubles every streetlight, and he is not fooled by any of them.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes reflections and invents the driver's thoughts.

kept.text: Your spare umbrella is probably visiting someone.
Home, then. You can look for your dignity tomorrow.

unruled.text: The gutter is running like a river and it has already claimed a casualty.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: narrates gutter flow and the broken umbrella.

unruled.text: That umbrella fought the good fight until about half past nine.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: backstory for pictured umbrella remains a caption.

unruled.text: The storm water is heading for the sea and taking prisoners.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: dramatic runoff metaphor replaces everyday human consequence.

kept.text: Did you pack a second pair of socks for yourself?
Bell first. Sock negotiations afterwards.

unruled.text: The puddle outside the gate is now part of the curriculum.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: curriculum joke directly labels the school-gate puddle.

unruled.text: Biggest attraction at the school gate this morning: forty square metres of weather.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: inventories this school-gate scene.

unruled.text: The bell can wait; the puddle has everyone's full attention, marshal included.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes the visible group admiring the puddle.

kept.text: Hair plans: cancelled.
Your hair appointment now feels rather optimistic.
Quick dash. You have never timed one correctly.

unruled.text: The newspaper got a promotion: today it is a roof.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: promotion joke directly describes the makeshift newspaper roof.

unruled.text: Fifty metres, two heels, one newspaper: the rain picked the wrong athlete.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: inventory and athletic flattery caption the woman.

kept.text: The view will keep while you find a towel.
Outing over. Everyone has a different version.

unruled.text: The sea is delivering the storm in person today, one wall at a time.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: dramatic sea description leaves the reader out.

unruled.text: High tide, big swell, and the front row is exactly as wet as it looks.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: explicitly describes what the viewer can see.

unruled.text: The boats knew. That is why they are all inside the wall.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: gives visible boats an invented shared thought.

kept.text: The boss can hold the umbrella for once.
kept.fixedFrom: Two colleagues, one umbrella: the org chart means nothing out here.

kept.text: You wanted a shorter meeting. Now you're trapped.
kept.fixedFrom: Friday's last meeting is thirty metres of open car park, chaired by the rain.

kept.text: This is closer than you meant by team building.
Meeting done. Lift negotiations have just begun.

unruled.text: Half a suit dry each: the fairest deal this office has struck all year.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: clever office comparison still describes pictured half-dry suits.

kept.text: The match is over. Your washing has extra time.
kept.fixedFrom: Saturday sport in the rain: the washing machine is about to meet its opponent.

kept.text: Your team owes your washing machine an apology.
Kit off. Nobody is putting that in with the towels.

unruled.text: Match played, rain won, boots benched at the door.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: sport metaphor narrates the pictured discarded boots.

unruled.text: That kit tells the whole story: rain, mud, and a game that went ahead anyway.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: explicitly explains the kit's visible story.

kept.text: Watering can wait; you've done enough standing about.
Call later. The roof would like to finish speaking.

unruled.reason: R5 fails: personification explains the visible roof runoff.

unruled.text: Rain on a tin roof: the loudest quiet sound in the country.

unruled.text: The fern has waited all season for exactly this delivery.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: plant-delivery metaphor describes the watering.

kept.text: The person who mops would like a word with you.
Boots off first. This is apparently news again.

unruled.text: The boots came off exactly one metre too late, and the prints agree.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: visible boot prints supply the entire punchline.

unruled.text: The garden is drinking; the stoep is dripping; the boots are done for the day.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: inventory of garden, stoep and boots.

unruled.text: Boot prints on the tiles: evidence of one quick dash into the weather.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: explains exactly what the boot prints show.

kept.text: Whose turn is it to let the dog out, exactly?
Bedtime soon. The dog has one more request.

unruled.text: The streetlight is showing every drop and the frangipani is drinking every one.

unruled.text: The frangipani gets watered at midnight and the whole street smells of it by one.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: lyrical tree caption invents two precise times.

unruled.text: One warm window, one wet street: everybody is exactly where they should be.
unruled.reason: R2 and R5 fail: cosy postcard sentiment, no earned turn.

kept.text: Your roof has a longer story than you do tonight.
Lights out. Something still has plenty to say.

unruled.text: The gutter found its river voice at about eight and has not stopped since.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: gutter personification describes its visible flow.

unruled.text: Rain through a streetlight looks like static, and tonight the whole street is tuned to it.

unruled.text: The jacaranda is getting a night wash and the street is getting the runoff.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: narrates the tree and runoff.

kept.text: You can stop promising yourself an evening swim.

unruled.text: The pool is being topped up by head office tonight, free of charge.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: pool-top-up caption gives the sky an office.

unruled.text: Rain on a lit pool: ten thousand rings and not one swimmer.

unruled.text: The only thing swimming tonight is the water itself.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: wordplay describes the empty pool.

kept.text: Your evening walk can end at the front door.
Out for fresh air. Back for an entire outfit.

unruled.text: The sea is coming over the rail and the rain is coming down to meet it.

unruled.text: The last umbrella on the beachfront is closed, which is the correct call.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes the visible closed umbrella.

unruled.text: Salt spray from the front, rain from above: the promenade is fully surrounded.
